# Insider Flow Report: NVIDIA CORP (NVDA)

**2026-05-30 to 2026-08-28** · 22 Form 4 filings read · 0 open-market buys ($0) · 3 open-market sales ($189,343,801)

# INSIDER FLOW REPORT — NVIDIA CORP (NVDA)
## Form 4 filings, 2026-05-30 through 2026-08-28

---

## SNAPSHOT

Twenty-three Form 4 filings fell inside the window; 22 were read and parsed, yielding 24 non-derivative transactions and no derivative transactions in the parsed material [23]. The composition is heavily mechanical: 13 grants/awards [A], 5 tax-withholding dispositions [F], 3 gifts [G], and just 3 open-market sales [S].

- **Open-market buys: none.** Zero shares, zero dollars, zero insiders.
- **Open-market sales: 3 transactions, 900,500 shares, $189,343,801, by 2 insiders** — both non-employee directors.
- **Net open-market flow: −$189,343,801.**

Essentially all of that net figure — 98.2% — comes from a single director on a single day. There were no open-market purchases or sales by any NVIDIA executive officer in the window; officers appear only via awards and tax withholding.

---

## OPEN-MARKET BUYS

None. No insider reported an open-market purchase [P] of NVIDIA stock in this window. That removes the strongest signal Form 4 data can offer — a cluster of insiders committing personal cash — and it is simply absent here.

---

## OPEN-MARKET SALES

Two directors sold, on separate dates, and there is no meaningful clustering: the sales are two weeks apart and the size disparity is roughly 57-to-1.

**Mark A. Stevens (director) — 2026-06-18 — 885,000 shares — $185,999,938.** Reported in two blocks on the same filing: 319,385 shares at a weighted average of $209.6952 ($66,973,501), leaving 5,772,886 shares, and 565,615 shares at $210.4372 ($119,026,437), leaving 5,207,271 shares [18]. This is the dominant event of the quarter by a wide margin. The associated holdings rows show a large remaining position: 11,543,401 shares held directly as of the 2026-06-23 report, plus 15,017,750 shares held indirectly by the Envy Trust and 5,207,271 shares held indirectly by trust [18], [10]. Stevens also received a routine 1,211-share director award on 2026-06-25, after which direct holdings were reported at 11,544,612 shares [10]. The parsed material for these filings does not carry a 10b5-1 footnote for the Stevens sales; note that such plans can exist without being flagged in the extracted data, so the absence of a note is not evidence either way.

**Stephen C. Neal (director) — 2026-06-03 — 15,500 shares — $3,343,863** at a weighted average of $215.7331, leaving 116,135 shares reported after the transaction [22]. Neal's later filing reports indirect positions of 116,135 shares (Neal/Rhyu Revocable Trust), 42,203 shares (2013 Stephen C. Neal Revocable Trust) and 7,142 shares (2013 Michelle S. Rhyu Revocable Trust) [6]. He too took the standard 1,211-share director award on 2026-06-25 (5,098 shares direct after) [6]. No 10b5-1 note appears in the parsed material for this sale.

Both directors sold at prices in the ~$210–$216 range and both retained multi-million-dollar or, in Stevens' case, multi-billion-dollar aggregate exposure after selling — a point worth weighing against the headline dollar figure.

---

## AWARDS, EXERCISES AND WITHHOLDING (context, not conviction)

**Director awards.** On 2026-06-25 nine directors each received an identical 1,211-share grant [A] at $0: Dabiri [5], Neal [6], Shah [7], Lora [8], Hudson [9], Stevens [10], Seawell [11], Jones [12] and Coxe [13]. The uniformity and single date mark this as the scheduled annual board equity grant, not discretionary buying. Suzanne M. Nora Johnson received two grants on 2026-08-10 — 1,262 shares and 1,148 shares — leaving 1,262 and then 2,410 shares reported [2], consistent with a newer or off-cycle board grant; she also reports 2,496 shares held indirectly by trust [2].

**Officer award.** Scott Gawel (Principal Accounting Officer) received two grants on 2026-06-08, 45,643 shares and 13,866 shares, at $0 [21]. These are awards, not purchases.

**Tax withholding.** On 2026-06-17, five officers had shares automatically surrendered at $207.41 to cover taxes on vesting equity [F] — a non-discretionary event, not a sale decision: Jen-Hsun Huang, 45,723 shares ($9,483,407), 70,146,252 shares direct after [19]; Colette Kress, 40,746 shares ($8,451,128) [15]; Ajay Puri, 36,927 shares ($7,659,029) [16]; Timothy Teter, 35,742 shares ($7,413,248) [14]; Debora Shoquist, 35,012 shares ($7,261,839) [17]. Combined, about 194,150 shares ($40.3m) left insider hands through withholding — but none of it reached the open market as a discretionary decision, and it is excluded from the net flow figure above.

**Gifts.** Tench Coxe reported two 500,000-share gifts [G], on 2026-07-01 (25,171,360 shares after) [4] and 2026-08-05 (24,671,360 shares after) [3]; both filings carry a 10b5-1 plan reference in the parsed material. Jen-Hsun Huang reported a 400,000-share gift on 2026-06-16, with 468,131,547 shares held indirectly by trust after [20]. Gifts are transfers, not sales; no proceeds accrue to the insider and no shares are necessarily sold into the market. Coxe made no open-market purchase or sale in the window.

**Option exercises.** The parsed material records none, and the derivative table is empty. Treat that as a limit of this dataset rather than a finding.

---

## WHO IS TRADING

**Directors** account for 100% of open-market activity — both sellers, Stevens and Neal, are non-employee directors — and for all 13 awards and all three gifts. Directors are also where the largest reported positions sit: Coxe (25,671,360 shares by trust plus 4,852,480 by profit-sharing plan trust) [13], Stevens, Jones (6,933,280 by living trust) [12] and Seawell (2,500,000 by survivor trust) [11].

**Executive officers** — Huang, Kress, Puri, Teter, Shoquist, Gawel — did no open-market buying or selling in this window. Their only appearances are the 2026-06-17 tax withholdings [14–17], [19], Gawel's 2026-06-08 awards [21], and Huang's gift [20]. That an entire senior management team, including the CEO and CFO, transacted zero shares on the open market over a three-month window is itself the notable structural feature of the quarter.

**10% holders.** None appear in the parsed material.

---

## SIGNAL READ

The honest reading is that this is a **thin, mechanically dominated quarter with one large, idiosyncratic director sale**, and it should not be over-interpreted.

Three points anchor that view. First, the net −$189m is not a broad insider verdict: it is two directors, and one of them (Stevens) supplies 98% of the dollars in a single day [18]. Two sellers two weeks apart, at different scales, is not a cluster; clustered *buying* is the stronger signal in Form 4 data, and there is none here to read. Second, the operators were quiet. No executive officer made a discretionary trade; the ~$40m of officer share dispositions on 2026-06-17 was automatic tax withholding at a single $207.41 price [14–17], [19], which is a vesting artifact, not a view on valuation. Third, both sellers retained large positions — Stevens still reports over 31 million shares across direct and trust holdings after selling [18], [10] — which is far more consistent with portfolio diversification or estate/liquidity management by long-tenured venture-background directors than with an exit.

The Coxe and Huang gifts are likewise not sales [3], [4], [20]; they reduce reported holdings without generating proceeds, and are commonly charitable or estate-planning transfers. Reading them as bearish would be an error.

**Caveats.** Form 4 covers only officers, directors and 10% beneficial owners — it says nothing about institutional flow or non-reporting holders. Filings are due within two business days, so this is near-real-time but not instantaneous, and it discloses transactions, never motive. Sales may be executed under pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 plans; the parsed material flags such a plan only on the Coxe gift filings [3], [4], and plans may well exist behind the Stevens and Neal sales without appearing in the extracted footnotes. One of 23 in-window filings was not read, and the derivative table came back empty — both are gaps in this dataset, not statements about the company or any insider.

Net: directional insider signal here is weak. Absence of buying is unremarkable at a company where compensation is equity-heavy and insiders are already saturated with stock; the selling is concentrated, non-executive, and against very large retained stakes.

*This is not investment advice.*
